Silhouette vs. Pirouette: What Changes When the Vanes Open?

By John Crawford Company · December 14, 2026

A still photograph only shows one setting of a sheer shade. To understand the difference between Hunter Douglas Silhouette and Pirouette, it helps to watch the fabric vanes open and close, then look through them from where you normally sit.

Both collections combine fabric with a sheer layer to manage daylight and privacy. The way the vanes are arranged gives each a different appearance. That is the most useful place to start a Silhouette vs. Pirouette comparison.

The fabric is arranged differently

The fabric is arranged differently
FeatureSilhouette Sheer ShadesPirouette Sheer Shades
ConstructionS-shaped fabric vanes between two sheer layersFabric vanes attached to a single back sheer
Vane sizes2, 3 or 4 inches5 inches
Open appearanceTilting vanes create spaces for filtered viewsFabric vanes change shape to reveal the back sheer
Room-darkening optionSelected Duolite or A Deux configurationsOptional A Deux configuration
What to compare in personVane spacing, fabric and the view through the sheersThe broader fabric vanes, their movement and the view

Silhouette creates a repeated horizontal pattern

Silhouette Sheer Shades hold their S-shaped fabric vanes between front and back sheer layers. Tilting the vanes changes the light passing through and your view outside.

The choice of vane size affects the scale of the treatment. A wider vane produces a different pattern across the window from a narrower one. Consider that pattern alongside window divisions, nearby shelving and other horizontal lines already in the room.

It is useful to view the sample from more than one position. What looks open when you stand directly in front of the window may read differently from a sofa or an adjoining room. Your normal viewing position should be part of the comparison.

Pirouette changes shape as the vanes open

Pirouette Sheer Shades use fabric vanes with a single sheer backing. Their broader vanes change shape as they open, giving the fabric a dimensional appearance. When comparing the two products, watch this movement rather than judging them only when fully closed.

Pirouette's 5-inch vanes create a different visual scale from the available Silhouette sizes. The fabric itself matters, too. A smooth material and a more visible texture can give the same construction a different character.

Neither appearance is automatically the better match for a large or small room. Consider how much you want the treatment to stand out and whether its pattern works with the furnishings you already have.

Compare the view and privacy as separate needs

Open vanes allow a filtered view through the sheer fabric. That view changes with the selected material, vane position and lighting. Ask to see the treatment both open and closed instead of assuming every sheer fabric will give the same result.

Evening privacy needs its own discussion. Tell us if the window faces a sidewalk, another house or an outdoor seating area. We can review what coverage you need when the room is lit and which configuration is appropriate.

A darker bedroom needs the right configuration

Both collections have selected configurations that combine the sheer treatment with a room-darkening roller behind it. Hunter Douglas offers Duolite or A Deux options for Silhouette and an A Deux option for Pirouette.

These are options to specify, not features to assume on every shade. We also consider light around the edges and the mounting arrangement when you want a darker room. Fabric, configuration and installation each contribute to the result.

Make the comparison from the room you use

Before choosing, note where you sit, when the sun is strongest and how often you expect to change the shade's position. Bring a photo showing the entire window wall so we can discuss the treatment alongside the rest of the room.
